what: The constructor discovers customer visited/location facts and the unique depot from grounded fact names, then reconstructs the complete directed routing-cost matrix from `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator metric costs. It resolves `load()` and optional exact `capacity()` numeric IDs once. Customer demands are obtained first from exact demand PNEs when present and, more importantly, structurally from the load assignment in grounded `visit-via-depot` operators; unavailable demands permissively default to zero. At evaluation, reusable buffers are filled with the current propositional and numeric state. The heuristic builds a capacity-aware nearest-neighbor completion from the current location: it repeatedly selects the cheapest remaining customer reachable directly when the estimated load permits, or through a depot reset otherwise, and finally adds the return-to-depot cost. Missing capacity disables the resource restriction rather than disabling routing estimation. All arithmetic is guarded and saturated to a finite non-negative value.
why: The CVRP state is fully characterized for routing purposes by the current location, visited set, load, and static directed travel costs. Grounded operator names and metric costs provide a reliable translator-independent way to recover those costs without parsing folded travel expressions or assuming symmetry. A constructive nearest-neighbor completion is inexpensive at O(n²) per state yet substantially more informative than customer counts or accumulated total cost because it reacts to spatial clustering, the current route endpoint, and the required final depot return. When capacity and demands can be recovered safely, modeling depot resets captures the dominant extra cost in low-capacity, multi-route instances; when they cannot, the same routing heuristic remains usable with permissive defaults.
